full_judgment:
9. Admittedly, the property has been listed as an abandoned property. Thus the onus lies upon the petitioner to rebut the presumption, provided in sub-section (2) of section 5 that the same was not an abandoned property. No oral evidence has been adduced before the settlement Court to prove that on 26-2-72 when President's Order 16 of 1972 was promulgated the original lessee, Naimuddin had been present in Bangladesh or his whereabouts were known or that he did not cease to occupy, supervise or manage in person the house in question. The Settlement Court upon assigning cogent reasons held that the kabala of the petitioner's vendor is forged and fabricated document and the original lessee, Naimuddin did never appear physically before any authority for any purpose after the liberation war in Bangladesh. The High Court Division has, thus, rightly, maintained the order of the Settlement Court by the impugned judgment and order. 

 11. In number of cases we have already decided that enlistment of a building under section 5 of the Ordinance shall retain its position as an abandoned property, in view of the provision of sub-section (2) thereof, unless the presumption is rebutted that the same is not an abandoned property within the meaning of Article 2 of President's Order No. 16 of 1972.
